FL-151.label: KV-cache optimization, usage accounting, and sticky sessions on one provider for cache benefits.
FL-151.walk: Send several messages in one thread; the spend module's KV cache column fills in after the first message and the provider stays the same across the thread.
FL-151.observed: All three fresh max-model tasks recorded 6,197 cached tokens on the second response, with one provider/model per thread; cache-acceptance.json preserves receipt lines.

FL-154.label: A model configuration and token cost policy per agent type: pinned, max, elbow or floor.
FL-154.walk: Open the agent-type config; each type (agent, sub-agent, curator) has its own token-cost policy set to one of pinned, max, elbow or floor.
FL-154.observed: Opened agent-type configuration: Agent, Sub-agent, Judge and Curator each expose their own pinned/max/elbow/floor policy. The case-sensitive text probe was false because headings render uppercase; the viewed UI and policy API show each role.

FL-155.label: An append-only spend ledger with fine-grain cost history, its smallest grain a spend unit with its own immutable id (a ULID, ADR-024 / A-027), and the spend views derived from it.
FL-155.walk: Send one message, then open the spend ledger; new rows with their own spend unit ids (ULIDs) appear beneath the unchanged older rows, and the spend module's totals add up from them.
FL-155.observed: Three fresh receipt runs proved new real ULIDs, unchanged old rows, stable ordering, exact receipt-derived totals and visible UI/API ID agreement. No additive UUID. Public 0.1.61 wheel also passed the append-only check; root capture is that released wheel.

FL-159.label: The spend module: a row per thread expanding to models, columns input / KV cache / reasoning / output / total / spend per hour, other costs as their own rows, scopable to a thread or stack.
FL-159.walk: Press the plus on one thread row in the spend module; it opens to that thread's models with the columns input, KV cache, reasoning, output, total and spend per hour, with an everything-else row beneath.
FL-159.observed: Three fresh runs expanded thread/model rows with input, cache, reasoning, output, total and spend/hour columns; real standalone embedding cost populated Other work. Scoped totals match receipt sums.

FL-197.label: Spend and Palace state reads use the calling principal; only the configured owner can request the whole Palace.
FL-197.walk: In a verification daemon, open Spend and Palace State and see only that principal's receipts and counts. In a local fixture, compare the configured owner's whole-Palace view. Request scope=palace as the verification principal and see a plain 403. Keep owner-rack captures out of evidence.
FL-197.observed: Second verification principal sees zero spend receipts and memory counts; scope=palace returns 403. Compared against the owner of this disposable test Palace only; no owner main-rack capture.

FL-169.label: Client and cloud versions stay sync-locked or backward compatible, following industry practice, so version differences feel seamless.
FL-169.walk: Start a client whose version differs from the cloud Palace's; it either keeps working or refuses with a plain version message.
FL-169.observed: Public 0.1.59 client and Memory wheels answered a real prompt against cloud Memory 0.1.61 / API 0.1.58. Then the public 0.1.61 pair passed the same-home reinstall and fresh receipt check.

FL-196.label: The rules machine checks citations, frozen law, product vocabulary, seed states and packet precedents.

FL-202.label: The model browser: every model the token source offers, ranked, pinnable, with price and context window; the thinking level beside it; the standard configurations one click away.
FL-202.walk: Open the model chip on a conversation: the source's models are listed ranked with price and context window; pin one and it stays on top; pick another and the thread switches to it and stays on it — new conversations start on it too, until you change it, and the chip says so; set the thinking level beside it; pick a standard configuration (pinned, max, elbow, floor) and see what it selects now; switching back from a model to a policy is one click.
FL-202.observed: Three fresh original model-browser runs passed all 16 checks: ranked catalog, price/context, pin ordering, selection, new-thread and restart persistence, thinking level, policy choices and /model.
